text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Dedicated pool 'eu-dedicated-03' p99 latency breach (streaming) detected. p95=480ms p99=2.4s, streaming stalls increasing. Alert rule: dedicated.streaming.tail_latency.p99 > 1.5s for 3m
anya (oncall): acked. I'm on it, joining call now. Can someone dump the pool metrics?
jordan: grabbing metrics, looks like queue depth spiked at ~11:12 UTC and warmup completed slowly for new workers. Autoscaler shows 2x scale requests in the last 4m, but handshake success delayed.
mike-sre: copying dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/pools/eu-dedicated-03
jordan: quick snapshot:
```
Time: 2026-03-15T11:12:00Z
pool_inflight_requests: 184
queue_depth: 120
avg_warmup_time: 28.2s
autoscale_request_count: 2
autoscale_latency_ms: 23000
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.42
streaming_stalls/sec: 12
p95: 0.48
p99: 2.37
```
anya (oncall): wow avg warmup ~28s, that explains tail. Are those new nodes using cold KV cache?
javier-eng-runtime: yes, the new hotshot workers come up cold by default. KV cache population is async; we've been seeing cold-path penalty when burst is >100rps.
sarah-prod: any customer-facing impact? Beth, CS — are you seeing support tickets?
beth-cs: we have two customers flagged as experiencing generation timeouts; both EU-region, both D2 Dedicated. One has reported degraded streaming (chunks arriving late). I've notified them and escalated.
anya (oncall): plan: 1) short-term: manual bump and route high-latency traffic to fallback model variant. 2) mid-term: reduce warmup cost and reduce autoscaler handshake time. Who can do manual bump now?
mike-sre: I can. I'll add +2 GPUs to pool eu-dedicated-03 and pin a warmup image with preloaded KV. Running command now:
```
$ infractl scale-pool --region eu-west --pool eu-dedicated-03 --delta 2 --reason "p99 tail mitigation"
Scaling request submitted: req-id=scale-98765
```
mike-sre: submitted. ETA for new instances ~45s-60s, warmup still needed. I'm also triggering a prewarm job to populate KV from recent prefixes.
javier-eng-runtime: I'll enable KV-prefetch for the pool until warmup stabilizes: toggling prefetch=true for pool eu-dedicated-03.
```
PATCH /api/pools/eu-dedicated-03/config
{"kv_prefetch": true, "kv_prefetch_sample_keyspace": "recent-1000"}
```
jordan: observing autoscaler logs: handshake failures correspond to TLS handshake timeout between controller and node due to kernel conntrack exhaustion. We're seeing a tail of failed registrations, causing autoscaler to retry and delay readiness.
anya (oncall): can we temporarily bypass autoscaler and allow immediate warm nodes to be attached?
mike-sre: yes, I can force-attach the two warmed instances once they boot. Marking them as ready to avoid the handshake path.
sarah-prod: also, can we route streaming requests for high-throughput customers to the compatible smaller model 'rwd-small-v2' until this stabilizes? It is CPU-friendly and has lower tail.
javier-eng-runtime: that requires a rollout config change for the route. I can do a canary redirect of 30% traffic for the affected routes. Applying route override now.
```
POST /api/route-overrides
{"route":"/v1/stream/generate","selector":"customer in (acct-203, acct-742)","model":"rwd-small-v2","percent":30}
```
anya (oncall): good. Beth, tell customers we're routing some requests to a lower-latency fallback to reduce stalls. Mention we expect full restoration in ~10-15m.
beth-cs: will send update.
jordan: metrics update 2m after manual actions:
```
Time: 2026-03-15T11:14:30Z
queue_depth: 54
pool_inflight_requests: 92
avg_warmup_time: 22.6s
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.27
streaming_stalls/sec: 5
p95: 0.39
p99: 1.15
```
anya (oncall): much better but p99 still borderline. Any remaining register failures?
jordan: handshake timeouts dropping, new nodes attached via force-attach, controller logs show lowered conntrack use after kernel tuning applied to ASG launch config (reduces netfilter conntrack boilerplate).
mike-sre: applied kernel sysctl changes in the launch template to bump net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max and reduce nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait. New instances will have that fixed.
javier-eng-runtime: follow-up: we'll add a short-term hotshot pool variant with prewarmed KV image for bursts >100. Proposal: auto-provision 2 prewarmed nodes per region and prefer them for handshake-critical requests.
anya (oncall): good idea. For now, let's monitor for 15 more minutes. I'll keep paging on until p99 < 800ms for 10 consecutive minutes. If it regresses, we escalate to SRE paging.
sarah-prod: also open a customer incident ticket and we should prepare a short RCA paragraph once we stabilize. Who owns the postmortem? I'm happy to own customer comms.
javier-eng-runtime: I'll lead the postmortem with runtime details and proposed mitigations (prefetch kv, reduce warmup, kernel tuning, autoscaler handshake improvements).
beth-cs: customers updated: "We've routed part of your traffic to a lower-latency model and provisioned extra capacity. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up."
jordan: final metrics at 11:26:
```
Time: 2026-03-15T11:26:00Z
queue_depth: 6
pool_inflight_requests: 28
streaming_stalls/sec: 0
p95: 0.32
p99: 0.62
```
anya (oncall): closing the active mitigation phase. Removed the route override (rolling back to original model) and scaling will be normalized by autoscaler.
javier-eng-runtime: rollback command executed for route override and scheduled a job to bake prewarmed images into the AMI for eu-dedicated pools.
mike-sre: I'll follow up with a runbook update to include force-attach steps and sysctl changes for the launch templates.
sarah-prod: filing incident ticket INC-2026-215 with summary, impacted customers, and mitigation timeline.
beth-cs: adding customer notes and next steps.
anya (oncall): thanks all. Postmortem owners: javier (runtime), mike (infrastructure), sarah (customer comms). I'll hand off to postmortem channel and mark the incident as resolved for paging. :thumbsup: 
incidents-bot: Incident resolved (duration 14m). Created incident record: INC-2026-215. Postmortem task assigned.
